h3. *Zimbabwe – Legal & Privacy Summary (Driver Safety Features)*

h4. 🔑 *Key Issue:*

Bolt intends to launch *Driver Selfie Verification* and *Driving License Verification* in Zimbabwe.

----

h3. 🏛️ *Legal Classification:*

* *Biometric data* (used in both features) is classified as *sensitive personal data* :dotted_line_face: under Zimbabwean law.
* This classification triggers *stricter compliance obligations*.

----

h3. :low_battery: *Requirements for Implementation in Zimbabwe:*

h4. ✅ *1. Written Consent (Lawful Basis)*

* *Explicit written consent* is required under *Section 12(1)* of the DPA.
* Consent must be obtained via a *clear affirmative action* (e.g. ticking a box) after proper notice.
* There are limited exceptions to consent (e.g. legal claims, public health), but *none currently applicable to Bolt’s use case*.

h4. 📩 *2. Prior Notification to the DPA (POTRAZ)*

* *Section 10(2)(d)* of the Regulations requires *prior notification* to POTRAZ for processing biometric data.
* *Format and procedure* for this notification are *not specified by law*.

# *Engagement with Local Legal Counsel* 🇿🇼

* We need to:
** Determine if any exemptions apply.
** Clarify the formal process and format for notification (not specified under current law).

----

h3. *What is next:*

* We should *initiate the DPA notification process*.
* *Local counsel should be engaged promptly* to avoid delays.

----

h3. *Compliance Risk:*

* *Non-compliance penalties* are severe:
** Include *financial fines* (unspecified).
** And *imprisonment of up to 7 years*.

h4. 📩 *2. Prior Notification to the DPA (POTRAZ)*

* *Section 10(2)(d)* of the Regulations requires *prior notification* to POTRAZ for processing biometric data.

* We should *initiate the DPA notification process*.

----

Hi, 

The Legal team has asked Commerce Compliance to assess whether in the Kaufman specific gift card based payment mechanism (see [op model visual|https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/10qgvjP6h64XEsnvDry7c2ZpAu6jfwBOR7lS3lZYcJyg/edit?slide=id.g326887b83aa_0_0#slide=id.g326887b83aa_0_0] ) Bolt can still benefit from PSD2 commercial agent exemption. 

Overall we are relying on the current legal assessment that the intended model is by nature agency model, meaning that the gift card issuing by Kaufland to Bolt does not impact this qualification. 

*In short*, we can remain relying on the PSD2 commercial agent exemption with the proposed model of using a gift card as payment mechanism to Kaufland. It is important to maintain the role of Bolt as only acting as agent of the merchant, whereas the User (client) should not be impacted by this scheme. 

*If this model is going to be implemented, please ensure the following*:

# Prepayment by Bolt to the gift card is made on account of Bolt’s own money.
# Advise to align with the Treasury and Finance teams on how the (pre)funding of this gift card will be ensured and to make sure that implementing the gift card model does not raise any operational risks for Bolt:
## there should always be a sufficient amount available on the gift card to cover all User payments (it should not look like the User is funding the gift card);
## Regarding making the prepayment by Bolt to the gift card. For the Bolt’s bank account from where we would fund the gift card - if it is going to be the same account where we receive the collected payment amounts from Users and make payouts to the partners - we need to have some system or controls in place to make sure that the amount we want to pay as prepayment for the gift card is available on the bank account. *We should to avoid a situation where we could be seen to use other partners (restaurants, couriers) money for the funding of the gift card.* 
# In contractual arrangements, make sure that User facing T&Cs will not be impacted from of anything relating to the gift card scheme between Bolt and Kaufman. Also, if possible in the agreements with Kaufland, let’s make sure that there are no references to Bolt potentially (re)distributing or giving a gift card (under Bolt’s gift card account) to the Users.

*Please also note* with this non-standard model, at this time we are not highlighting significant FinReg risk, but should we get any indication of such a scheme increasing the FinReg risk in Romania (or in the EU) we need to reassess our position.

I hope you’re doing very well.

We would appreciate your review and approval of the lease agreement for the new warehouse in Cyprus. For context, the landlord was not willing to use our standard lease template, so we had to work with theirs.

Please find below the links to:

* The *latest clean version* of the agreement
* The *original version with my proposed changes in track changes*, in case it's helpful for comparison.

The landlord has already accepted all of my proposed changes, except for the rent increase percentage. He remains firm on applying a 10% increase every two years. Please refer to the legal note below for further context regarding rent increase limitations.

*[*[*Link to Clean Version*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wGCgG-lLhSaMcT1zc89VhMO2Fkp73ghY/edit]*]*
*[*[*Link to Markup Version*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jsCpPXL1LpYw0xdSLto64LW0RpvEC9XA/edit]*]*



*Summary of Key Terms* 

*Term:*

* Initial term of *24 months and 2 weeks*.
* Agreement may be renewed for successive *2-year periods* under the same terms and conditions, unless either party gives *90 days' prior written notice*.

*Rent:*

* €14,400/year + VAT
* Paid monthly at *€1,200 + VAT*
* *Late payment interest:* 2% p.a. after 30 days from due date, subject to written notice.
* *Deposit:* One month’s rent (€1,200 + VAT)

*Termination:*

* Either party may terminate *for convenience* with *3 months' written notice* before expiry.
* Tenant must return the warehouse in its original condition, excluding normal wear and tear.
* Security deposit refundable within 30 days of termination, subject to deductions.

*Notable Rights and Obligations:*

* Tenant may use utilities and bring equipment.
* Owner must ensure uninterrupted utilities (especially electricity), and fix defects within 24 hours or Tenant may recover repair costs.
* Tenant must obtain necessary permits and licenses for use.
* Property cannot be used in a way that causes nuisance or disruption.

h4. 

----

*Legal Note - Rent Control Law in Cyprus*

While the landlord has pushed for a *10% increase every two years*, it’s important to note that properties located in *Nicosia*  -particularly older ones- *may fall under the Cyprus Rent Control Law*.

If the Rent Control Law applies:

* The *maximum allowable rent increase is 6% every two years*, as currently set by the Council of Ministers.
* Any increase above this could be considered unenforceable, and the tenant has the right to contest it before the Rent Control Court.

Although it’s not 100% confirmed whether this specific property falls within the scope of the Rent Control Law (as it depends on construction date and location), I recommend that we *push back on the proposed 10% increase* by citing the Rent Control Law and request that the increase be capped at *6%*.

If the landlord confirms that the Rent Control Law does not apply to this property, then we can reassess and potentially accept the 10% increase -which, in any case, appears commercially reasonable given the current rent level.

Would love to hear your thoughts!

Many thanks!

No, the missing of clause regarding the contract end date does not change the situation, because then the conditions of the General Terms shall apply. 

From a legal perspective, the terms of a signed contract may only be amended by the mutual written agreement of the parties, unless the contract itself expressly provides for a different mechanism or applicable legal acts permit unilateral amendments. However, such exceptions are typically narrowly defined and apply only in limited, specific circumstances, which this situation is highly unlikely to fall within.

To avoid similar issues in the future, I recommend updating the template of our individual contract to include a clause that explicitly allows for unilateral amendments initiated by Bolt, subject to clearly defined conditions and procedural safeguards.

*Research Summary*

*Thesis Title:* _Psychological Safety in a Multicultural Tech Company_
*Researcher:* Andres Kepler (EBS, Estonian Business School)
*Contact:* [andres.kepler@bolt.eu|mailto:andres.kepler@bolt.eu]

*Overview*
This bachelor thesis explores how engineers in multicultural, high-responsibility teams perceive psychological safety. The study focuses on communication, team dynamics, and leadership—especially during high-stress scenarios such as on-call duty and incident response.

The ultimate goal is to develop actionable insights that could support management in improving psychological safety practices across engineering teams.

*Purpose of the Survey*
The aim of the survey is to gather anonymous insights into team members’ perceptions of openness, trust, and cultural inclusion in technical settings.

*Survey Details*

* *Format:* Online (Google Forms, IP tracking disabled)
* *Estimated Time:* 5–10 minutes
* *Participants:* Pilot run with 8–10 engineers
* *Voluntary:* Participation is fully voluntary and anonymous
* *Data Collected:* General, non-identifiable demographics (e.g., role, nationality, preferred working language)
* *No PII Collected:* Names, emails, and IP addresses are not collected
* *Data Retention:* Deleted after thesis submission (latest by end of 2025)
* *Results:* Only anonymous aggregate summaries will be used in the thesis
* *Validation:* Survey questions will also be validated in consultation with the academic supervisor along with Bolt

While the questions and structure are designed to meet academic standards for a bachelor's level thesis, the small sample size of 8–10 individuals in a pilot makes it statistically insufficient to draw reliable conclusions. For example, a 40% response rate from this cohort would yield only 3–4 responses, which is too limited for meaningful analysis. Therefore, I kindly request support in expanding the survey audience to enable statistically valid insights. If permission is granted, I am planning to request additional approval from Engineering VP Toomas Römer to extend the survey across the broader engineering organization.

*Legal and Ethical Considerations*
The survey complies with GDPR under the legal basis of academic research (Article 89). Informed consent is obtained at the start of the survey. The project is coordinated with Bolt HR and Privacy stakeholders.

*Note*
The company will not be named in the final thesis title or any publicly visible documents. All materials will remain internal and academic unless explicitly approved.

----

h1. Survey: Psychological Safety in a Multicultural Tech Company

h2. Introduction

You are invited to participate in a survey as part of a bachelor’s thesis at Estonian Business School. The purpose of this study is to explore psychological safety and inclusion within multicultural tech teams. The findings will help inform practical tools and management practices to foster more inclusive and supportive workplaces.

h2. Consent & Confidentiality

Participation in this survey is voluntary. Your responses will be kept strictly confidential and used only for academic research purposes. You may skip any question or withdraw from the survey at any time without any penalty. No personally identifiable information will be included in the final report.

By continuing with this survey, you acknowledge and consent to the use of your anonymized responses for research purposes.

----

h2. Key Definitions

* *Psychological safety*: Feeling able to speak up with ideas, questions, concerns, or mistakes without fear of negative consequences.
* *Multicultural*: The presence and interaction of people from different national, linguistic, or cultural backgrounds within a team.

----

h2. Demographic Questions

# *How long have you worked with your current team or department?*
#* Less than 6 months
#* 6–12 months
#* 1–2 years
#* 2–5 years
#* More than 5 years
# *What is your current job role or title within the company?*
#* (Open text)
# *What is your primary working language at the company?*
#* English
#* Estonian
#* Russian
#* Other: ________
# *Which region or cultural background do you most identify with?*
#* Baltic/Nordic
#* Western Europe
#* Eastern Europe
#* Asia
#* Other: ________
# *What is your age group?*
#* Under 25
#* 25–34
#* 35–44
#* 45–54
#* 55 or older
# *What is your gender?*
#* Female
#* Male
#* Non-binary/Other
#* Prefer not to say
# *What is your work arrangement?*
#* Fully remote
#* Hybrid
#* On-site
# *How long have you been with this company?*
#* Less than 1 year
#* 1–3 years
#* More than 3 years

----

h2. Core Survey Questions

Please indicate your level of agreement with the following statements.
*Scale:* Strongly Disagree / Disagree / Neutral / Agree / Strongly Agree

# *In my team, I feel safe to express my honest thoughts, questions, or concerns.*
# *When mistakes are made in my team, they are treated as learning opportunities rather than reasons for blame.*
# *I feel comfortable asking teammates for help, even on issues outside my immediate responsibilities.*
# *Different viewpoints and cultural perspectives are welcomed and respected in my team discussions.*
# *During high-pressure situations (such as incidents or tight deadlines), I feel supported by my teammates.*
# *I trust that my team lead or manager will support me if I make a mistake or face a challenge.*
# *It is difficult for me to speak up in my team when I disagree with others.*
_(Reverse-coded: agreement indicates lower psychological safety)_
# *I have experienced challenges related to cultural differences or language barriers in my team.*
# *My team actively makes an effort to include members from different cultural backgrounds.*
# *To what extent do you feel that psychological safety in your team impacts your motivation, engagement, or performance at work?*

----

h2. Behavioral & Qualitative Questions

# *Have you ever withheld feedback or a suggestion out of fear that it might negatively affect you or your relationships within the team?*

* Yes
* No

# *What is one thing that management could do to improve psychological safety and inclusion in your team?*

* (Open text)

# *Please share any specific examples or comments related to psychological safety, inclusion, or cultural differences within your team.*

* (Open text)

----

h2. Optional: Follow-up

# *Would you be willing to participate in a brief follow-up interview to discuss your experiences in more detail?*

* Yes (If yes, please leave your preferred contact method: email or Slack handle)
* No

----

h2. Pilot Test Note (for Methodology Section)

{quote}This survey was pilot tested with a small group of colleagues (N=3) to ensure clarity and relevance. Minor wording adjustments were made based on their feedback.{quote}

----

h2. Survey References

Core psychological safety items are adapted from Amy Edmondson’s Psychological Safety Scale and recent literature on multicultural team dynamics.

* Edmondson, A. (1999). _Psychological safety and learning behavior in work teams_. Administrative Science Quarterly, 44(2), 350–383.
* Stahl, G.K., Maznevski, M.L., Voigt, A., & Jonsen, K. (2010). _Unraveling the effects of cultural diversity in teams: A meta-analysis of research on multicultural work groups_. Journal of International Business Studies, 41(4), 690–709.

----

*Thank you for your participation!*

* Might be too early to tell if these are early signs of under-performance, but this automation needs close monitoring.

The focus as of now is only on the 2nd query in this [+Databricks notebook here+|https://bolt-common.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/1734315320391047?o=3598988355446810#command/4594295929432777], which can be used to feed Braze with custom attributes.

* We’ve decided in favour for creating 2 separate custom attributes for soft bounces: invalid_email_address and mailbox_full (instead of only one soft_bounced custom attribute, which has different values).
* The logic behind both of the attributes would be as follows:
** When a user is soft bounced and the soft bounce reason is one of the two mentioned above (invalid_email_address or mailbox_full), the respective custom attribute should be set to TRUE.
** To clear the same attribute, null values would be sent instead of changing it to false. This way the custom attribute would be removed from the user entirely.
*** This is necessary, so the LCM could only rely on one definition in global liquid logic in Braze, instead of writing out all possible scenarios.
** The attributes would not be narrowed down for a couple of markets for PoC, but all the campaigns data will be looked at to get the best overview of the results.
** Once we add the custom attribute on the user profile, it should be kept there for 2 weeks and then rechecked.
** As of now, the updates would be manually via CSV after every 2 weeks. If it has good impact, then we’d go forward with the automation of the solution.

*Update 30.05.2025*

We concluded the post-analysis for 2/3 experiments concluded recently : 

[+2025-05 France Perform iOS (Partnership) Increase+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6342967481/2025-05+France+Perform+iOS+Partnership+Increase] : We observed *incrementality* in iOS sign-ups. The +3K daily spend generated 251 daily signups, iGMV/Cost = 7.4. However, note that if we use *"local user sign-ups"* as the measurement metric (instead of total sign-ups), we don't [observe any incrementality for the increased spend|https://bolt-datascience.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/2447439818255477?o=3829506390716583#command/2447439818255478]. This finding solidifies our hypothesis that tourists are significantly influencing our incremental experiments. This is problematic because the models mistakenly equate uplift from tourists with incremental ad uplift. Therefore, all the uplift for this experiment may not be coming from the increased spend. So, the incremental uplift observed should be taken with a grain of salt. 
The [project|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/MARTECH3-715] to recommend a holistic solution for the "tourist problem" in ads measurement is still in this year's MarTech agenda.

[+2025-05 Ukraine BCN Android (Partnership) Increase+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6342968059/2025-05+Ukraine+BCN+Android+Partnership+Increase] : *No incrementality* observed on android signups for +3K daily budget. The partner struggled to reach the required spend, was only able to reach 400 euros/daily while the minimum budget was 3K euros/daily.

[+2025-05 DE Perform iOS (Partnership) increase+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6357712898/2025-05+Germany+Perform+iOS+Partnership+Increase] : The results are *inconclusive*. We didn't observe any significant uplift from the +€2K daily spend increase. However, Meta iOS spend dropped from over €700 daily to just over €200 daily between May 13 and May 19, 2025, which may have impacted the experiment. This makes the experiment invalid, and we recommend conducting a drop test later.

*Next Steps*

* Analyse rest of the experiments after completion, 
* Agree with the ads team on the budgets and experiment plan for partnership channels in Q3

{noformat}WITH overcharge_check AS 
	(
	SELECT 
		oc.calculation_date,
		oc.order_token_id,
		oc.city_id,
		oc.decision,
		oc.rule_name_array,
		oc.prediction_price_local,
		oc.actual_price_local,
		oc.prediction_price_eur,
		oc.actual_price_eur,
		oc.user_id,
		CASE WHEN cardinality(filter(oc.rule_name_array, x -> x LIKE '%RECALCULATE_ZERO%')) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS recalc_to_zero,
    	row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST(oc.order_token_id AS varchar)||CAST(oc.city_id AS varchar) ORDER BY oc.calculation_id DESC) AS rownumber
	FROM ng_public.etl_driver_overcharge_check oc
	WHERE oc.created_date  >= DATE_ADD('month',-3, current_date)
	AND oc.calculation_date >= DATE_ADD('month',-3, current_date)
	),
flags AS 
	(
	SELECT 
		foc.order_id,
		foc.city_id,
		foc.user_id,
		foc.created,
		foc.created_date,
		approx_distinct(CASE WHEN facr."type" IN ('RIDE_TOO_SHORT_TIME','RIDE_DID_NOT_HAPPEN','DRIVER_DID_NOT_PICK_UP_RIDER','DRIVER_DID_NOT_MOVE','GPS_UPFRONT') THEN foc.order_id END, 0.0041) AS flag_for_rdnh,
		approx_distinct(CASE WHEN facr.is_fraud = 1 THEN facr.id END, 0.0041) AS fraud_flagged
		FROM ng_public.fraud_order_check as foc
		LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.fraud_order_check_result as facr ON facr.order_check_id=foc.id AND facr.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -4, current_date) as date)
		WHERE foc.created_date >= DATE_ADD('month',-4, current_date) AND foc.created >= DATE_ADD('month',-4, current_date)
		GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
	)
SELECT 
--date_trunc('month', co.created) AS month_created,
co.country_code,
round(sum(COALESCE(co.user_price_eur,0))) AS sum_user_price_eur,
round(sum(COALESCE(co.partner_price_eur,0))) AS sum_partner_price_eur,
round(sum(COALESCE((co.refund_amount/co.eur_currency_rate),0))) AS sum_refunds_eur,
round(sum(CASE WHEN COALESCE((co.refund_amount/co.eur_currency_rate)*1.00/co.user_price_eur,0) > 0.9 THEN COALESCE((co.refund_amount/co.eur_currency_rate),0)END)) AS sum_full_refunds_eur,
approx_distinct(co.order_id,0.0041) AS count_orders,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN co.refund_amount > 0 THEN co.order_id END,0.0041) AS count_refund_orders,
approx_distinct(CASE WHEN COALESCE((co.refund_amount/co.eur_currency_rate)*1.00/co.user_price_eur,0) > 0.9 THEN co.order_id END,0.0041) AS count_full_refund_orders
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS co  
LEFT JOIN flags f 
  ON f.order_id = co.order_id AND f.city_id = co.city_id 
  AND f.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) AS date)
LEFT JOIN overcharge_check AS oc ON oc.order_token_id = co.order_id AND oc.city_id = co.city_id AND oc.calculation_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month',-3, current_date) AS date) AND oc.rownumber = 1
LEFT JOIN ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r on co.price_currency  = r.currency and DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE (co.created) - INTERVAL '2' DAY
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month',-3, current_date) AS date) 
  AND co.order_state = 'finished' AND co.order_type ='rides'
--AND co.driver_id = 5359229
AND f.flag_for_rdnh > 0
AND oc.decision = 'pass'
AND co.payment_method_type <> 'default'
--LIMIT 3000
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC{noformat}

Hi [~accountid:712020:36cbea54-0723-40fc-a8d1-2d4945acece1] as informed over Slack: 

*Court Decision on Stockholm Permit Allocation Appeal*

We have received the decision from the Administrative Court regarding our appeal. Unfortunately, *the court has rejected it*.

*Court decision in short*:

* While the court agrees that the City's explanation for allocating e-scooter permits is unclear and inconsistent (_which is good_), it concluded this does not prove the City considered irrelevant factors.
* This outcome is disappointing, especially given the court's reasoning. It seems contradictory to require us to prove the City acted improperly, while also accepting that the City’s rationale is not transparent.
* The ruling in full can be read _here_:
** [Swedish original version|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1yJRuJ5YYuuqPnDZhTrRy_osRZOxX40GJ/view?usp=drive_link]
** [English AI translated version|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1eWhLXsx6x6HxvH7wC-f4nSBS-Cp0hdTX/view?usp=drive_link]

*Next steps*:

* We now need to consider whether to appeal to the Court of Appeal in Stockholm. The deadline is June 19. An appeal requires leave to appeal, which typically takes 1–2 months to process. There’s no urgency from Snellman's side, so they recommend internal discussions before we decide how to proceed.
* When I spoke with Snellman about our appeal prospects, they believe leave to appeal is likely, but estimate only a 30% chance of the decision being amended. However, the City's acknowledgment that the previous allocation system was flawed may work in our favour (especially if we have this in writing), as well as that the court at least acknowledged that the allocation made was inconsistent and unclear.

Let me know your initial thoughts. I'm happy to schedule a call next week to discuss further, if you'd like.

There are *legal and reputational aspects* to consider when associating the Bolt brand with an alcohol brand.

h4. 1. *Is it legally permissible in Paraguay?*

* Advertising of alcohol is regulated under Law No. 1333/98 and subsequent resolutions.
* Promotions involving alcoholic products (raffles, giveaways, etc.) may be restricted—especially if:
** Targeted at younger demographics
** Promoted on social media without clear age-gating
** Presented as “incentives” for purchasing or engaging with services
* Check if the beer brand is legally compliant and licensed to advertise and promote in this manner.

h4. 2. *Reputational risk?*

* Even if legally permissible, such a campaign might:
** Be misinterpreted as encouraging alcohol consumption
** Risk negative perception in more conservative sectors or among regulators
** → To be discussed with PR?

Hi [@richard.chahine|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U03HDDEG9A9], please find below my recommendations after having review the in-app flow that is used in Portugal.Ideally, after the rent is finished we should (i) present the user with the exact amounts that they will be charged, and (ii) proceed with charging only after we have their explicit consent.However, taking into account the market practice in Poland and the current app flow in Portugal, I confirm that the Portugal model can be used for Poland as well, under the following conditions:

# Explicit consent for the deposit is collected at the beginning of the rental. The summary about the rental and the deposit should include a clear reference to the relevant T&Cs outlining the charges that may be imposed on the user - I believe that in the current structure only a reference to the FAQ about the deposits are made.
# The payments are transparently outlined in the summary after the rental is completed. What is more, any incompliance forming basis for charges should be duly documented and a clear reference to ours and Interfleet’s T&Cs should be made at this stage as well. Having analysed the Portugal model, I understand that this is already applicable there.
# The term for users objection should be prolonged to 14 days (as it is a market practice and is a customary deadline for the consumer in Poland; this is already regulated in the Interfleet’s T&Cs in that way).
# After 14 days, the funds should be either released (to avoid unnecessary blockages on the users’ accounts) or charged according to the provided summary of the additional costs (see point 2 above).
# The user should have a right to object/file a complaint (through CS or otherwise). Having analysed the Portugal model, I understand that this is already applicable there.

Hope the above clarifies your doubts, otherwise, please feel free to reach out. Thank you!

** [+Slovakia - Bratislava, Tiktok Conversion, Android.+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6338674914/2025-05+Bratislava+Slovakia+-+TikTok+Android+Spend+Increase] _The results are inconclusive due to negative incrementality and a flat model curve, likely caused by the low number of daily leads register via the Driver Portal. ** [+Poland - Warsaw, Tiktok Conversion, Android+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6346932225/2025-05+-+Warsaw+Poland+-+TikTok+Android+Spend+Increase]. _Same with Slovakia, Bratislava. Try to measure using geolift with Krakow and Trojmiasto as counterfactual cities, identified probability of incrementality impact by 84%,_ [+_notebook_+|https://bolt-datascience.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/753604058260776?o=3829506390716583#command/753604058260834]
** [+_France - Paris,Tiktok, OS-Based Android_+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6338413214/2025-05+-+Paris+France+-+TikTok+Android+Spend+Increase]_. No incrementality detected for the experiment in this geo and channel_ 
** [+Azerbaijan - Baku, Google, Android, Youtube Reach+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6314524673/2025-04+-+Baku+AZ+-+Youtube+Reach+Android+Spend+Increase]. _No incrementality detected with a probability of impact being 55%._
** [+Nigeria - Abuja, Google, UAC OS+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6338773044/2025-04+-+Abuja+NG+-+Google+UAC+Android+OS+Spend+Increase]. Launching Google UAC with a €150 daily spend led to an average uplift of 34 Step 2 leads (+31%), with an iCPA of €4.38 and an incremental GMV-to-Cost ratio of 3.9. However, uplift trends began 5- 6 days before launch, likely influenced by other ongoing Meta CLS experiments. While power analysis suggests conditions were met and CLS was assumed to be fairly distributed across OS, it’s possible the uplift from CLS impacted Android more, as ~85% of drivers in Abuja use Android.
** [+Lithuania - All cities, Google UAC+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6345916439/2025-05+-+All+Cities+LT+-+Youtube+Android+Spend+Increase]. _No incrementality detected for the experiment in this geo and channel_

{code:sql}-- Gather collected fee per driver. Looks like fleets are not affected.
with collected_amount as (
    select
        from_agent_id as driver_id,
        billing_profile_id,
        SUM(sum_with_vat) as sum_with_vat
    from
        ng_public.billing_ride_hailing_record
    where
        created_date >= DATE('2025-05-31')
        and handling_timestamp >= timestamp '2025-06-01 America/Asuncion'
        and handling_timestamp < timestamp '2025-06-02 America/Asuncion'
        and billing_profile_id in (
            548602,
            548595,
            548601,
            548599,
            548600,
            548604,
            548633,
            548642,
            548637,
            548638,
            548645,
            548634,
            548644,
            548647,
            548636,
            548646,
            548641
        )
        and type = 'fee'
        and from_agent_type in ('driver')
    group by
        1,
        2
),
-- Get Old and new commission percentage
fee_config as (
    select
        fc.company_id,
        fc.id,
        fc.start_date,
        fc.end_date,
        cr.id is not null as is_company,
        cast(
            coalesce(
                JSON_EXTRACT(cr.data, '$.percentage'),
                JSON_EXTRACT(dr.data, '$.percentage')
            ) as DOUBLE
        ) as percentage
    from
        ng_public.invoicing_fee_calculator fc
        left join ng_public.invoicing_fee_calculator_company_row cr on cr.fee_calculator_id = fc.id
        left join ng_public.invoicing_fee_calculator_driver_row dr on dr.fee_calculator_id = fc.id
    where
        fc.company_id in (
            select
                company_id
            from
                ng_public.invoicing_fee_calculator
            where
                id in (
                    548602,
                    548595,
                    548601,
                    548599,
                    548600,
                    548604,
                    548633,
                    548642,
                    548637,
                    548638,
                    548645,
                    548634,
                    548644,
                    548647,
                    548636,
                    548646,
                    548641
                )
        )
        and (
            end_date = DATE('2025-06-01')
            or start_date = DATE('2025-06-01')
        )
    order by
        fc.company_id,
        fc.id,
        fc.start_date,
        cr.classname,
        dr.classname
),
-- Connect old and new percentage
fee_config_v2 as (
    select
        fc1.company_id,
        fc1.is_company,
        fc1.id,
        fc1.percentage as new_percentage,
        fc2.percentage as old_percentage
    from
        fee_config fc1
        left join fee_config fc2 on fc1.start_date = fc2.end_date
        and fc1.company_id = fc2.company_id
    where
        fc1.start_date = DATE('2025-06-01')
        and fc1.percentage is not null
        and fc2.percentage is not null
),
-- Get collected sum, and diff to compensate
sums as (
    select
        driver_id,
        billing_profile_id,
        sum_with_vat as collected_sum_with_vat,
        sum_with_vat / fc.new_percentage * fc.old_percentage as should_ve_collected_sum_with_vat,
        sum_with_vat - (
            sum_with_vat / fc.new_percentage * fc.old_percentage
        ) as diff_to_compensate
    from
        collected_amount ca
        left join fee_config_v2 fc on ca.billing_profile_id = fc.id
)
select
    *
from
    sums;{code}

The timeout is set as follows:
- if no extra options timeout provided in the request it is set to the client’s one here: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/a4f19bcc17826b0ad89c2a3b04292e24402e42c8/src/httpOutgoing/ExternalRequestClient.ts#L3468|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/a4f19bcc17826b0ad89c2a3b04292e24402e42c8/src/httpOutgoing/ExternalRequestClient.ts#L3468] 
- if no request timeout provided in the client it is set to the global one (currently, 5 seconds) here: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/a4f19bcc17826b0ad89c2a3b04292e24402e42c8/src/httpOutgoing/ExternalRequestClient.ts#L369|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/a4f19bcc17826b0ad89c2a3b04292e24402e42c8/src/httpOutgoing/ExternalRequestClient.ts#L369] 

So, by providing {{extraOptions}} parameter we’re to set custom timeout for a particular api call

- On 4 June BG expects to receive a positive assessment from the European Central Bank and the European Commission;
- If it receives a positive assessment, it should receive the approval of all member states by July.

*Update 02/06*

Additional experiments measured by [~accountid:712020:902d65c1-f6d8-4b16-8d42-efa2808ca034]:

* [+2025-05 Norway blackout test+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6344343818/2025-05+Norway+blackout+test]. *No incrementality.* That’s the first ever in-house blackout test for Norway, aimed at determining whether ads have a statistically significant impact at all. As the budgeting process for Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 unfolds, the recommended spending levels have been notably low, raising concerns about the overall effectiveness of performance marketing in that market. The results of the tests suggest that there is no evidence of any monetary return on our investments. Therefore, we should consider shutting down all BAU channels until further proof is provided. P.S. I even tried to run the post analysis for Oslo separately hoping that would make any difference, but sadly not.
* [+2025-05 Poland Meta iOS increase+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6346539417/2025-05+Poland+Meta+iOS+increase]. *No incrementality.* A 2k increase daily in spend didn’t result in any statistically significant uplift in signups. Not even close. The market conditions held quite well in the pre-analysis phase, no evidence of external factor interruption. The results of the study should therefore be trusted. Therefore, Meta iOS for Poland should be considered as a low efficiency channel. In case of discrepancies between these results and the ones we are going to get from our MMMs a deeper analysis should be conducted.
* [+2025-05 Cyprus TikTok iOS launch+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6346834054/2025-05+Cyprus+TikTok+iOS+launch]. *Incrementality*. An increase in 550EUR daily resulted in 48 statistically significant signups with average ROI 6.0 which is an outstanding result among in-house studies. We both observed an incrementality and didn’t overspend during the experiment period. However, a couple of important considerations to keep in mind:
** Cyprus is a highly touristic market where only 20% of the new signups are coming from locals. The signup uplift is coming mostly from the tourists, post-analysis without tourists gave no incrementality.
** When a tourist season starts the flows of Android and iOS tourists increase at different pace, usually with a bigger iOS share. That increases the chance to observe false positive result when using iOS as a target platform and Android as a counterfactual.
** Therefore, while the results of the experiment suggest a high efficiency of TikTok iOS, I would suggest considering that with some grain of salt.
* [+2025-05 Nairobi Meta Android increase+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6346899584/2025-05+Nairobi+Meta+Android+increase]. *Incrementality*. Daily increase by 800EUR results in 223 incremental signups with average ROI of 3.8 which is a pretty good result for in-house counterfactual study. No issues during the pre-analysis stage and an extremely low p-value indicate a small chance of observing a false positive result.
* [+2025-05 Madrid Google Android launch+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6346834488/2025-05+Madrid+Google+Android+launch]+.+ *Incrementality*. An increase in 1400EUR daily resulted in 52 incremental signups with average ROI 2.58, which is most probably above-the-target spend but generally OK for experiment purposes. No issues at the pre-analysis stage and low p-value indicate low chance of observing a false positive result.

{noformat}def match_curves_to_experiments(exp_df, post_ext, show_plot):
    rows = []
    for os, channels in post_ext.items():
        for channel, values in channels.items():
            channel_name = f"cost_{os}_{channel}"
            vmax_mean = values['vmax_mean']
            rows.append({'channel': channel_name, 'vmax_mean': vmax_mean})

    vmax_df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    vmax_df['vmax_mean'] = vmax_df['vmax_mean'].round(2)

    exp_df_enriched = exp_df.merge(vmax_df, on='channel', how='left')

    exp_df_enriched['curve_delta'] = exp_df_enriched.apply(
        lambda row: abs(
            mm_saturation(row['cost_before'], row['vmax_mean'], row['vmax_mean']) -
            mm_saturation(row['cost_after'], row['vmax_mean'], row['vmax_mean'])
        ),
        axis=1
    )
    exp_df_enriched['curve_delta'] = exp_df_enriched['curve_delta'].round(2)

    if show_plot:
        for channel in exp_df_enriched['channel'].unique():
            df_channel = exp_df_enriched[exp_df_enriched['channel'] == channel]
            vmax_mean = df_channel['vmax_mean'].iloc[0]

            # Generate cost range for curve
            max_x_val = max(exp_df_enriched['cost_after'].max(), exp_df_enriched['cost_before'].max())
            x_vals = np.linspace(0, max_x_val * 1.2, 300)
            y_vals = [mm_saturation(x, vmax_mean, vmax_mean) for x in x_vals]

            # Plot curve
            plt.figure(figsize=(5, 3))
            plt.plot(x_vals, y_vals, label='mm_saturation curve', color='blue')

            # Plot dots for each experiment
            for _, row in df_channel.iterrows():
                y_before = mm_saturation(row['cost_before'], row['vmax_mean'], row['vmax_mean'])
                
                # Defining y_after:
                if row['cost_after'] > row['cost_before']:
                    y_after = y_before + abs(row['delta'])
                else:
                    y_after = y_before - abs(row['delta'])

                plt.scatter(row['cost_before'], y_before, color='red', zorder=5)
                plt.scatter(row['cost_after'], y_after, color='red', zorder=5)
                plt.plot([row['cost_before'], row['cost_after']], [y_before, y_after], color='gray', linestyle='--', linewidth=1)

            plt.title(f"Saturation Curve and Dots - {channel}")
            plt.xlabel("Cost")
            plt.ylabel("Saturation")
            plt.legend(loc='lower right')
            plt.grid(True)
            plt.tight_layout()
            plt.show()

    return exp_df_enriched{noformat}

Hi [~accountid:5b7d01f0b57ed25933f642e0], I've reviewed the *Dubai Information Security Regulation* (ISR v3.1) shared by DTC:

*Findings*

* The Regulation introduces a data localisation requirement — but it *only applies to* _“_*_classified data_*_”_, which is defined as "_non-public information explicitly designated as sensitive or confidential_ {{by the government entity itself}}".
* *The classification decision therefore rests with DTC*. That gives us some strategic room to work: not all user or operational data will necessarily be considered “classified”.  However, we need to keep in mind that the DESC can audit DTC, as a Government entity in Dubai.
* *No blanket restriction on accessing data from outside the UAE* — remote access (e.g. by HQ teams in Estonia) is not prohibited in these Regulations, provided adequate security and access controls are in place
* *No requirement to store all data in the UAE* — only data classified as “classified” needs to be localised. Everything else can remain in our existing infrastructure

*Next steps*

* We should engage with DTC to help them make those distinctions (between _Classified_ and _Non-Classified_ data) clearly and proportionately. DTC will likely get its own legal interpretation done.
* From my review of this specific Regulation, the localisation requirement is a manageable and contained requirement, assuming DTC doesn’t apply an overly broad classification.
* I believe AWS has a Region in the UAE, which we could leverage for any data that DTC does choose to classify as 'Classified'.

Thanks.

h2. *For easier understanding: Summary of User Deletion Process in Bolt’s Admin:*

# *Initiation by Support Agent*:
A Customer Support Agent initiates a user deletion request through the Admin interface.
# *Admin Sends Deletion Request*:
The Admin system sends a deletion command to the internal User service via the endpoint {{/admin/gdpr/delete}}.
# *Eligibility Check*:
The User service first checks whether the user is eligible for deletion (e.g., ensuring there are no unresolved obligations or pending legal holds).
# *User Data Deletion*:
If eligible, the User service deletes the user's personal data from the main user database ({{user-db}}).
# *(Optional Internal Steps)*:
Any internal steps required after deletion (such as cleanup or confirmation) are handled within the service.
# *Deletion Event Published*:
The system then publishes a "user deleted" event to an internal event queue, which can notify other systems (e.g., analytics, compliance, fraud detection) to also delete or anonymize related data.
# *Confirmation to Admin*:
The Admin system receives confirmation that the user has been deleted.
# *Confirmation to Agent*:
The Customer Support Agent is notified that the deletion process has been successfully completed.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
h3. *Important Clarification on Scope and Limitations*

* The *diagram represents a high-level overview* of the deletion process specifically for certain user types (e.g., riders and eaters) via the Admin interface.
* *Only a limited subset of personal data* is deleted through this flow — primarily data stored in the core user database.
* *Other teams and systems* may subscribe to the deletion event and take further action to delete additional data, but this is *not guaranteed across all systems*.
* The deletion of data held in *external systems or tools* (e.g., marketing communications platforms) follows *separate processes* not shown in this diagram and is documented elsewhere.
{panel}

Hi [~accountid:63fe21787c30bbd6b33e09d3](please don’t look at this whilst on holiday - definitely one for your return from leave! 🙂). I’ve set out a draft response below, but would appreciate a look-over please before I give the go-ahead. Ultimately, I think the introduction of a reservation fee for scheduled rides is low risk on the basis that TfL has no say in our pricing and (from carrying out research) there are no UK regulations that preclude this. 

*Draft Response*  

Hi Olabowale and Debbie

Many thanks again for raising this query with the legal team. In short, on the basis that TFL have no say in our pricing, the introduction of a reservation fee is low-risk, and we have set out our thoughts in response to each of your questions below: 


# *Can Bolt legally introduce a reservation fee for riders? This fee would be charged at the point of scheduling a ride.*

_Yes, since TfL doesn’t regulate pricing, Bolt can charge a reservation fee to riders_ *_provided that:_*
-  _the fee is clearly disclosed to the rider_ *_before booking_*_;_
-  _rules around whether or not the reservation fee is refundable are explained to riders_ *_before booking_*_;_
-  _the fee does not mislead the passenger as to what the fee covers (e.g. it does not guarantee a driver)._  
# *If possible:*
*a. Can Bolt keep 100% i.e Is it permissible to charge the rider this fee without sharing any portion of it with the driver?*

_Yes, in principle. Although the_ [_driver terms_|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-drivers/] _and the_ [_passenger terms_|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/legal/terms-for-riders/] _don’t give us the explicit right to do so at this stage (as the reservation fee is a new feature), we could rely on the following clauses/principles to charge the rider this fee and not share any portion of it with the driver:_

_-_ _clause 6.1 of the driver terms states that drivers authorise Bolt as their commercial agent to receive any “_*_other fees_* _paid by the Passenger via In-app Payment and to forward_ *_relevant funds_* _to [the driver]” (emphasis added)._ +_We could argue that we are not sharing any portion of the reservation fee on the basis that they are not “relevant funds”._+ 
- _under the driver terms, the “Fare” is defined as “the fee a Passenger is obliged to pay Driver for provision of the Transportation Services”. Since the reservation fee is a new charge and not directly tied to the service provided by the driver, it does not fall under the definition of “Fare”. We could therefore argue that Bolt is not contractually obligated to share this fee with drivers._ 
- _the passenger_ _terms state that a service fee may be charged to riders. We could therefore treat the reservation fee as a service fee that is not part of the driver fare._ 

_The_ *_risk of not sharing any portion of the fee with the driver is that we may open ourselves up to driver complaints around transparency of fees._* _Ideally, if introduced, the terms would be updated to reflect this fee to avoid any disputes from drivers/riders._ 

*b. Share between Bolt & drivers i.e Alternatively, if legally required , can the fee be split between Bolt & Driver. (Would we just charge service fee as we do with Cancellation fees)*

_Yes. There is no legal requirement to do this, but it may make sense from a fairness standpoint._ 

*c. Can the Driver keep 100%*

_Yes. Though note that this may be viewed as part of the “trip earnings” in HMRC/tax reporting so this should be disclosed clearly in driver comms._ 

Thank you

Hello [~accountid:712020:49595943-fb9f-4151-8a74-b00c57b18f30] !

This contract can be deceiving, as it does not contain the correct wording and it refers to ‘denúncia’ when, in reality, there is no possibility of early termination, but only opposition to renewal.

The contract is valid for a period of two years, with automatic renewal for the same period if neither party objects to the renewal (clause 12). It seems to us that it is not possible to terminate it earlier, but only to oppose to the renewal.

This opposition to renewal should be made by registered letter, sent 90 days before the date on which the initial period of the contract ends and on which automatic renewal would take place.

In other words, as the contract is dated 11/02/2025, its initial period ends on 11/02/2027.

If Bolt wishes to oppose to the automatic renewal, it must send a registered letter to Central Med by 11/11/2026 (but if by that time we already know we want to terminate the contract, I advise to send this letter at the beginning of November 2026 and not just on the 11th, so that there is no doubt as to the deadlines and compliance with them).

Clause 13 of the document provides that, in the event of non-compliance with the previous clause, i.e., untimely termination of the agreement, Bolt undertakes to pay Central Med, as compensation, the amount corresponding to two annual fees.

Despite not being possible to terminate the contract before the ending of it’s initial period of two years without any specific reason (which is what we call “denúncia”), it is possible, as in any contract, to terminate it on the grounds of breach of contract (“resolução).

However, in order to proceed with that termination, it is necessary to demonstrate that Central Med has breached the contractual obligations it assumed and agreed to comply with.

In your ticket, you mention that we are not satisfied with their service, but this is different from a breach of contract.
Therefore, if you wish, you can specify the reasons for our dissatisfaction and/or indicate whether there has been any breach of Central Med's obligations and, if so, which ones, and we will then be able to assess whether there are grounds for “resolução”.

In either case, we suggest sending written communications to Central Med expressing our dissatisfaction or the reason why we believe they are not complying with the contract. That is always important in order to “create” evidence if it becomes necessary.

Tell me if you need anything else regarding this topic!

Thank you!

h3. Investigation Summary

* When capturing a bundle booking, we create a task called {{CAPTURE_BOOKING_FUSE}}, which is intended to handle payment allocation for the associated bundled bookings.
* Currently, within the {{CaptureFinishedTask}} class that processes the {{CAPTURE_BOOKING_FUSE}} task, there is an attempt to allocate payment to the bundle booking itself instead of the individual bundled bookings. This misallocation leads to the error {{capture_result of booking must not be null}} in Kibana.
* To resolve this issue, we need to update the code [here|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/platform/commerce/balance_user/main/service/task/CaptureFinishedTask.ts#L117] to ensure that payment is correctly allocated to the associated bundled bookings.

h3. Next Steps

# Replicate this bug in the prelive environment.
# Test the fix in the prelive environment.
# Deploy the fix to the live environment.

+*PRIVACY ANALYSIS*+

* No new categories of personal data are being processed here. Similarly, no new purposes / legal bases.
** We already process data for the purpose of reporting safety incidents. Only change here is that the rider can now do it in real time, in a way that is anonymised and passed on to the driver in a quicker manner.
** Data being processed is proportionate for the purposes being pursued.
* We have the usual minor transparency gap regarding the driver privacy notice, but this is being addressed in the coming weeks (I have made some minor tweaks to the draft). We can for now maintain that this is covered in the current driver privacy notice.
* DPIA not required here.
** Processing not likely to result in bias / discrimination / significant effects, and no practical effects on the driver other than a warning.
** Steps are being taken to anonymise the report coming from the rider, and so no obvious risk to the rider’s wellbeing.
** No explicitly special category / criminal offence data being processed here, nor any data of vulnerable individuals.
** Also data is being processed on a large scale, we are already processing it.
** Personal data is coming directly from the rider, and being passed on to the driver. As such, processing is within the users' expectations.
* No ADM risk. Feedback provided by the user, and no effect for the driver.
* Regarding DSARs, we would approach these as we would approach any other safety reports (to the extent such data is retained). Users will not be able to object.
* No obvious third parties involved in the processing.
* No obvious overlap with the ICO investigation.

+*CONCLUSION*+

* Overall risk profile = {color:#36b37e}*Low*{color}
* We can proceed with this initiative, including in the UK (/) 
* Worth just asking how  is this data stored on the driver’s / rider’s profiles (although this is not a blocker).

*RE: Confirmation Regarding the Acceptance of Option Agreements on the ShareForce Platform*

Dear Mr. Marko Kõiver,

I am reaching out to you on behalf of our client, Bolt Technology OÜ (hereinafter “Bolt”), regarding the digital signing of option agreements.

To date, Bolt has used the Carta platform ([https://carta.com/uk/en/|https://carta.com/uk/en/|smart-link] ) to manage its option grants and has previously received confirmation from the Estonian Tax and Customs Board (hereinafter “ETCB”) that the digital acceptance of option agreements via Carta constitutes a valid digital signature. As such, these agreements have not needed to be submitted to the ETCB within five working days, as would otherwise be required under § 48(5³) of the Income Tax Act.

Bolt is currently transitioning to a new option management platform, ShareForce ([https://www.shareforce.net/|https://www.shareforce.net/|smart-link] ), and wishes to continue following the same procedure—namely, that separate submission of signed option agreements to the ETCB would not be required, provided that the new platform ensures a comparable level of reliability and verifiability to what the ETCB has accepted in its previous practice.

Below is a simplified overview of how the ShareForce platform operates in relation to the signing of option agreements:

* The identity of the employee is verified prior to signing through either:

* the ShareForce login system (SSO – Single Sign-On), or
* two-factor authentication (2FA – e.g. password + confirmation code via phone).

* When the employee agrees to the terms of the option agreement (by clicking “Accept” on the platform), the system records:

* the exact date and time (in UTC),
* the user's unique identifier (account information),
* the IP address (network address from which the signature was made),
* information about the device and browser used to sign the document,
* and a digital fingerprint of the document (a cryptographic “hash” that proves the document has not been altered after signing).

* After signing:

* neither the document nor its associated data can be modified or deleted, not even by system administrators,
* all data related to the signing is stored in log files (audit logs), which can be exported in CSV or Excel format if needed,
* version history of the document is preserved in a secure file server (e.g. AWS S3), where nothing is overwritten or deleted.

All these measures are intended to ensure that it is possible to reliably verify who signed which document and when, and to confirm that the content has not been modified after signing.

We note that the acceptance given on the ShareForce platform does not formally meet the definition of an “advanced electronic signature” (AES) under the EU eIDAS Regulation. However, it does resemble a so-called “simple electronic signature” (SES), which the ETCB has accepted in practice—provided that the time of signing and the identity of the signatory can be reliably verified, and the signing process is auditable.

Based on our firm’s previous experience (e.g. with Carta, Personio, Fidelity, E*Trade), we kindly request that the ETCB confirm whether acceptance via the ShareForce platform would be sufficient to consider an option agreement digitally signed, and thus exempt from the requirement to submit the agreement to the ETCB within five working days.

Bolt intends to transition to the ShareForce platform in the near future and to continue issuing options. We would therefore greatly appreciate your response at your earliest convenience.

If desired, I am happy to provide further background over the phone.

Sincerely,
Tõnu Kolts
Attorney-at-Law

By the end of the day, it seems that we are not yet ready to come-up with a script that can perform fully automated inference about noise and uncertainty.

GaussianRegressor gives help in assessing the Lengthscale and Variance, but it also tends to overlearn and requires manual boundaries to be set.

For example, 

* it would very often start to assess AR-noise (which we assume to have ls 15+ days) as random noise (basically adjusting to ls=2)
* sometimes it would also overestimate the variance making it too large (so that it is visibly unrealistic)

So for now the status is:

* We have some semi-manual process (described [here|https://github.com/bolteu/data-analytics/blob/master/marketing/martech-automation/simulations/Parameter%20Inference.ipynb]) to assess the *var* and the *ls.* 
* But it still relies on some assumptions and subjective choices. 
* We agree that it will be enough for now, but in the future we will spend more time assessing approach to uncertainty and DGP in general.



While working with GP regressor, we:

* learned to work with GPRegressor and designed the function to make it most clear and simple possible (we have two functions - {{infer_ar_noise}} and {{generate_ar_noise_with_gp}}, using the same GPregressor interface
* checked how random state works there (and ensured we are getting different time-series)
* checked that auto-correlation often follows our settings of LS (but not var)
* Imputing noise on android gives the same result as imputing the scaled noise on iOS (i.e. they are symmetrical)
